newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine fin min orders SEC to nab speculators.
newsitem.headline: Philippine fin min orders SEC to nab speculators.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Wednesday that he had ordered stock market regulators to use the "full force of the law" to punish anyone found to have manipulated share prices.
In a statement, de Ocampo reiterated government insistence that there was no fundamental economic reason for the recent drop in share prices and that the market and economy were sound.
The local stock index has slumped about 16 percent since early April, initially on fears of an impending property collapse.

"(De Ocampo) suspects that rumours of a collapse in the property industry were planned to cause panic reaction, leading to the stock fall...there is good reason to suspect that the stock market behaviour in late April and early May was abnormal," his department said in a statement.
"(He) has ordered the Securities and Exchange Commission not to spare anybody and to use the full force of the law to rid the stock market of manipulators," the statement said.
On Tuesday, the Philippines' SEC announced it had launched what it called a "discreet inquiry" into possible market rigging.
"De Ocampo said he is looking at the possibility of short-selling where some smart stock players make money from falling stock prices," the statement added.
